model.shop.dim_customers.compiled_code:
select
    c.customer_id,
    c.first_name,
    c.last_name,
    c.email,
    c.city,
    c.signup_date,
    coalesce(co.order_count, 0) as order_count,
    co.first_order_date,
    co.last_order_date
from "shop"."analytics"."stg_customers" as c
left join "shop"."analytics"."int_customer_orders" as co on c.customer_id = co.customer_id
model.shop.dim_customers.name: dim_customers

model.shop.dim_products.compiled_code:
-- select * on purpose: whatever staging exposes, the dimension exposes.
-- Convenient, and exactly the kind of thing that hides a dropped column.
select
    *,
    case
        when unit_price >= 200 then 'premium'
        when unit_price >= 50 then 'mid'
        else 'budget'
    end as price_tier
from "shop"."analytics"."stg_products"
model.shop.dim_products.name: dim_products

model.shop.fct_orders.compiled_code:
with paid as (
    select
        order_id,
        sum(amount) as amount_paid,
        count(*) as payment_count
    from "shop"."analytics"."stg_payments"
    group by order_id
)

select
    t.order_id,
    t.customer_id,
    t.order_date,
    t.status,
    t.gross_amount,
    t.discount_amount,
    t.net_amount as net_revenue,
    coalesce(p.amount_paid, 0) as amount_paid,
    coalesce(p.payment_count, 0) as payment_count
from "shop"."analytics"."int_order_totals" as t
left join paid as p on t.order_id = p.order_id
model.shop.fct_orders.name: fct_orders

model.shop.int_customer_orders.compiled_code:
select
    customer_id,
    count(*) as order_count,
    min(order_date) as first_order_date,
    max(order_date) as last_order_date
from "shop"."analytics"."stg_orders"
where status <> 'cancelled'
group by customer_id
model.shop.int_customer_orders.name: int_customer_orders

model.shop.int_order_totals.compiled_code:
with items as (
    select
        oi.order_id,
        sum(oi.quantity * p.unit_price) as gross_amount
    from "shop"."analytics"."stg_order_items" as oi
    inner join "shop"."analytics"."stg_products" as p on oi.product_id = p.product_id
    group by oi.order_id
),

orders as (
    -- discount is a rate (0.10 = 10% off), not an amount; naming it that way here
    select
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        status,
        discount as discount_rate
    from "shop"."analytics"."stg_orders"
)

select
    o.order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_date,
    o.status,
    coalesce(i.gross_amount, 0) as gross_amount,
    round(coalesce(i.gross_amount, 0) * o.discount_rate, 2) as discount_amount,
    coalesce(i.gross_amount, 0) - round(coalesce(i.gross_amount, 0) * o.discount_rate, 2) as net_amount
from orders as o
left join items as i on o.order_id = i.order_id
model.shop.int_order_totals.name: int_order_totals

model.shop.mart_customer_ltv.compiled_code:
-- LTV here is cash actually collected (payments), not booked revenue,
-- because returns and unpaid orders make booked revenue optimistic.
-- Cut-offs put roughly the bottom and top fifth of the sample data in low and high.
select
    c.customer_id,
    c.email,
    c.signup_date,
    c.order_count,
    coalesce(sum(f.amount_paid), 0) as lifetime_value,
    case
        when coalesce(sum(f.amount_paid), 0) >= 6000 then 'high'
        when coalesce(sum(f.amount_paid), 0) >= 2500 then 'medium'
        else 'low'
    end as value_tier
from "shop"."analytics"."dim_customers" as c
left join "shop"."analytics"."fct_orders" as f on c.customer_id = f.customer_id
group by c.customer_id, c.email, c.signup_date, c.order_count
model.shop.mart_customer_ltv.name: mart_customer_ltv

model.shop.mart_daily_revenue.compiled_code:
-- Net revenue is spread across an order's lines by their share of gross,
-- so a discounted order doesn't make one category look better than it is.
with lines as (
    select
        f.order_date,
        dp.category,
        oi.quantity * dp.unit_price as line_gross,
        f.gross_amount,
        f.net_revenue
    from "shop"."analytics"."fct_orders" as f
    inner join "shop"."analytics"."stg_order_items" as oi on f.order_id = oi.order_id
    inner join "shop"."analytics"."dim_products" as dp on oi.product_id = dp.product_id
    where f.status in ('completed', 'shipped')
)

select
    order_date as revenue_date,
    category,
    count(*) as line_count,
    sum(line_gross) as gross_revenue,
    round(sum(case when gross_amount > 0 then net_revenue * line_gross / gross_amount else 0 end), 2) as net_revenue
from lines
group by order_date, category
model.shop.mart_daily_revenue.name: mart_daily_revenue

model.shop.stg_orders.compiled_code:
-- The source system has written every status spelling it could think of.
select
    id as order_id,
    customer_id,
    order_date,
    case
        when lower(trim(status)) in ('completed', 'complete') then 'completed'
        when lower(trim(status)) in ('cancelled', 'canceled') then 'cancelled'
        else lower(trim(status))
    end as status,
    coalesce(discount, 0) as discount
from "shop"."analytics"."orders"
model.shop.stg_orders.name: stg_orders

model.shop.stg_payments.compiled_code:
select
    id as payment_id,
    order_id,
    method as payment_method,
    cast(amount / 100.0 as numeric(12, 2)) as amount
from "shop"."analytics"."payments"
model.shop.stg_payments.name: stg_payments
